rows.analysis: Pre-June 13, 1979 multi-unit buildings in Outer Sunset (94122) are governed by SF Rent Ordinance rent control and just-cause eviction rules, superseding California AB 1482's 8.8% cap (Civ. Code §1947.12(d)(3)).

rows.category: Mandatory Pre-Condition: SF Rent Increase License
rows.official_value: Annual March 1 Housing Inventory report required (§37.15)
rows.analysis: Owners of 1–9 unit SF buildings must maintain a current Housing Inventory filing and active Rent Increase License before imposing any §37.3(a)(1)–(2) annual or banked increase; unlicensed increases are suspended.

rows.category: Unit 1 Anonymized Recommendation (Alex Morgan & Casey Kim)
rows.analysis: Official value blank (conditional on unverified private lease): Recommended uniform 1.6% annual increase = +$63.92/mo → $4,058.92/mo (or on Feb 1, 2027 exact anniversary: 1.4% banked + 1.6% current = 3.0% / +$119.85 → $4,114.85/mo), ONLY after confirming April 1, 2026 continuing tenancy is month-to-month rather than a fixed term through March 31, 2027. Zero roommate/vacancy reset permitted while original tenant Alex Morgan remains.

rows.category: Unit 2 Anonymized Recommendation (Riley Chen & Quinn Patel)
rows.analysis: Official value blank (conditional on unverified private rent ledger): Recommended uniform 1.6% current annual increase = +$50.40/mo → $3,200.40/mo on 30/35-day written notice, leaving up to 11.5% ($362.25/mo) lawfully banked without expiring. Theoretical 13.1% max (+$412.65 → $3,562.65/mo if zero increases since June 1, 2019) requires 90/95-day notice (mail cutoff Nov 25, 2026 for Feb 28, 2027) and carries high tenant-counsel audit risk.

rows.category: Corporate REITs vs. Individual SF Property Owners
rows.official_value: §37.10C bans algorithmic rent software ($1,000/unit/mo penalty); 2–4 unit owners = 14.6% of U.S. properties (DSCR 74 vs. 164 for 50+ units)
rows.analysis: Institutional landlords use systematic annual CPI notices and formal passthrough petitions (while barred from algorithmic pricing under §37.10C and DOJ antitrust enforcement); small individual owners more often defer annual increases for retention, accumulating banked balances and risking §37.15 licensing oversights.

rows.official_value: Written notice: 30 days (≤10%) / 90 days (>10%); +5 calendar days by CA mail
rows.analysis: Serve written notice personally or by first-class U.S. Mail (never email/text alone), itemizing base rent, current annual %, banked % with exact anniversary dates (Rule 4.12(b)), and §37.15 compliance. Keep the $29.50 (50% of $59) Rent Board Fee strictly separate from base rent.

rows.category: SF Tenant-Lawyer Scrutiny & One-Unit vs. Both-Units Verdict
rows.official_value: Uniform neutral policy across covered units defeats disparate-treatment claims (42 U.S.C. §3604; Gov. Code §12955; Civ. Code §§51, 1942.5)
rows.analysis: Applying a documented, uniform building-wide policy (1.6% annual CPI adjustment to BOTH Unit 1 and Unit 2 on each unit's earliest lawful eligibility date, after confirming zero open habitability citations or 180-day repair complaints) neutralizes selective-targeting, retaliation, and fair-housing inquiries.
